facts.text: GymnasiumEnv is the gymnasium.Env view of a bigym.loco controller-in-the-loop environment; the adapter owns no physics and reports everything from the wrapped environment
make_gym(task_name) builds GymnasiumEnv(make(task_name, config, **overrides)); it does not call gymnasium.make
The action space is a Box that copies the wrapped environment's low, high and shape
step casts the action to float32, reshapes it to the action space and clips it into the action space before stepping the environment
The observation space is a Dict with an rgb uint8 0..255 field and a state float32 field
reset(seed=s) passes the seed to the wrapped environment; a reset without a seed draws one from the adapter's np_random
A step returns terminated = last and discount == 0, and truncated = last and not terminated
The observation returned by reset and step is a dict with rgb and state arrays
The render metadata is render_fps = round(1 / control_step_seconds)
The step info carries success, fell, event_progress and discount, and a terminal step adds termination and truncation_reason
The default camera keys are head, right_wrist and left_wrist
The default state keys are proprioception, proprioception_grippers and proprioception_floating_base
The episode budget is in inner environment steps and one outer control step is demo_down_sample_rate inner steps; the default 10 is 50 Hz
The default camera shape is 84x84 and the default frame_stack is 1
The outer action dimension is the outer base slots plus the selected limb actuators plus the gripper count
The outer action space is Box(-1, 1) over the computed action dimension
The low-dim observation length is summed over the configured state keys and frame-stacked
The rgb observation space is uint8 0..255 with shape (num_cameras, 3 * frame_stack, H, W)
The task drawer_top_open is registered with DrawerTopOpenG1 and a 13500-step budget
The default robot is the Unitree G1 with Dex1-1 parallel two-finger grippers
The G1 MJCF is bigym/envs/xmls/g1/g1_29dof_with_dex1_1.xml with model name g1_29dof_with_dex1_1

determinism.notes: reset(seed) pins the fake's initial state and the fake advances it deterministically; the upstream environment draws its episode seed from numpy and simulates with MuJoCo, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the fake and upstream

fidelity.engine: bigym2:gym_adapter (fake backend: kinematic stand-in for the MuJoCo bigym.loco environment)
gaps: kinematic fake: the fake backend advances a placeholder state directly and models no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors or noise; the upstream bigym.loco environment is a MuJoCo rigid-body simulation (bigym/envs/xmls/g1/g1_29dof_with_dex1_1.xml:1) and was not run here

the fake observation is a 3-channel 4x4 rgb placeholder plus a 12-value state; the upstream default rgb observation is 3 cameras x 3 channels x 84x84 uint8 and the state length is summed over the configured state keys (bigym/loco/config.py:33,154-156,164; bigym/loco/env.py:1011-1056)
the fake action vector is 24 placeholder values; the upstream action length is computed from the robot's selected actuators and the controller (bigym/loco/env.py:921-923,1004-1009)
no rendering: the fake implements no render() and returns no image
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
the fake was not compared with the upstream environment: the upstream package is not installed where the gate runs and package code never imports the clone
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
